subject: forestSpirit
pitch: A small forest spirit, part deer and part mossy stone. A body of grey river stone covered in soft green moss, slender wooden legs ending in little hooves, branching antlers sprouting tiny white flowers and leaves, a pale wooden mask-like face with two glowing green eyes, and a few fireflies circling its head.
reasoning:
I'm sketching out a compact deer spirit design—a small quadruped around 0.9m tall with a simple hips-to-chest spine chain, keeping the body geometry minimal using basic stone shapes.

For the limbs I'm planning IK leg chains ending in cone or box hooves, a neck-to-head chain with a jaw joint for the mask-like face, glowing green eye spheres, and antler sweeps branching out with small flower clusters and leaf details. Fireflies will be simple emissive spheres attached near the head bone, sharing a glow material to keep things efficient.

Now I'm working out the exact joint coordinates for the hips, chest, and spine chain using catmull-rom points, making sure the root joint and parent-child naming line up correctly.

I'm defining the body sweep with mottled stone-and-moss paint layered via countershade, plus scattering moss lumps, small stones, and a few white flowers across the back for texture. For the legs, I'm calculating hip and foot positions per side and figuring out the segment lengths for a three-joint limb chain that reaches from hip height down to the hoof.

Naming the four joint points per leg with side suffix L for the mirrored set, parenting front legs to the spine and hind legs to the hips. Setting up the sweep geometry for the legs...

I'm adding a dark hoof at the foot tip using a tapered cylinder positioned at the bone's end, with stone-textured spheres placed at the shoulder and hip joints for the haunch detailing. Now I'm plotting the neck chain as a curve running from the upper body up to the head base.

Next I'm defining the head joint angled forward and tilted down from the neck, then building the skull using a frustum-box shape stretching from the head's center outward to form the face, with a separate frustum planned for the upper jaw.

I'm adding the lower jaw joint and its frustum shape, then layering in facial details—a dark nose sphere, brow ridge rods, glowing green emissive eye spheres set in darker eye socket spheres, and dark mask-line accents.

Now I'm sketching leaf-shaped ear extrudes, moss tufts from small spheres, and working through the antler geometry—carefully resolving left/right coordinate direction relative to the head joint, then sweeping a catmull curve through points computed from the head's local space to form each antler branch.

Now I'm planning flowers at the antler tips and along branches, with small squashed spheres for leaves, and a simple flower function using five white petal-spheres ringed around a yellow center. I'm keeping part counts manageable, roughly six parts per flower across about ten flowers per antler, so total stays reasonable.

I'm settling on colors: warm brown wood, white petals with golden centers, green leaves. For fireflies, I'm placing small glowing spheres in a circle around the head bone with slight height variation, considering a second larger pale sphere for a halo effect.

I'm adding a small tail as two chained joints off the hips, curving down and back, and extending the spine with hip and chest spheres of varying radii to shape the rump and body. I'm checking proportions so the whole creature stays compact, with antler tips topping out around 1.6 units high.

Now I'm setting up roles for the jaw and head joints, then adding wood grain texture along the legs and pale flat coloring for the body. For the moss I'm scattering small lumps across the body surface with randomized scale and a couple of green shades, filtering by surface normal so they land on upward-facing areas, and considering a few grey stone accents near the flank before deciding to keep things simple with flat shading.

Next I'm building out the sweep for the spine using the bone chain, attaching ears as scaled, rotated spheres for a leaf-like shape, and placing the eyes and eye sockets on the head using local offsets—bright green eyes set slightly forward with darker, slightly larger sockets recessed just behind them to match the skull's width.

Still working out leg and hoof placement...
